Rashi on Chullin 19b:10:1.hebrew: שחט במקום נקב נעשה כמי ששחט עובד כוכבים - חצי קנה, וגמר ישראל, דקא נפקא חיותא בידא דישראל. ובפלגא קמייתא לא מיטרפא, דפסוקת הגרגרת שיעוריה ברובא:
Rashi on Chullin 19b:10:1.english: If he slaughtered at the place of a perforation, it is as though a gentile had slaughtered - [The gentile slaughtered] half of the windpipe, and an Israelite finished [it], since the life departs at the hands of an Israelite. And it is not rendered a *tereifa* by the first half, because [in the case of] a severed windpipe, its measure is [determined] by a majority.

Rashi on Chullin 19b:10:2.hebrew: שחט ופגע בו נקב נעשה כמי ששחט ישראל וגמר עובד כוכבים - דפסול, דהא לא עביד ישראל שיעור שחיטה ברישא:
Rashi on Chullin 19b:10:2.english: He slaughtered and a perforation struck it; it is treated as though a Jew slaughtered and a gentile finished - That it is invalid, since the Jew did not first perform the required amount of slaughter.

Rashi on Chullin 19b:10:3.hebrew: קרי עליה - רבי יוחנן על רבי אלעזר:
Rashi on Chullin 19b:10:3.english: He recited about him - Rabbi Yochanan [recited a verse] about Rabbi Elazar:

Rashi on Chullin 19b:10:4.hebrew: עובד כוכבים עובד כוכבים - לא שהיה קורא לו "עובד כוכבים", אלא ליגלג עליו: "עובד כוכבים, עובד כוכבים!" כלומר, בשחיטת עובד כוכבים אתה תולה טעמך, וכל היום אתה יכול לומר "עובד כוכבים, עובד כוכבים", ואין הטעמים דומים, כדמפרש רבא:
Rashi on Chullin 19b:10:4.english: "A idolater! A idolater!" - It is not that he was calling him "an idolater"; rather, he was mocking him: "Idolater, idolater!" That is, you base your reasoning on the slaughter of an idolater, and all day long you could say "idolater, idolater," but the reasons are not comparable, as Rava explains.

Rashi on Chullin 19b:11:1.hebrew: בשלמא - שחט ישראל וגמר עובד כוכבים, פסולה:
Rashi on Chullin 19b:11:1.english: Granted - [in the case where] a Jew slaughtered and a gentile finished, the slaughter is invalid.

Rashi on Chullin 19b:11:2.hebrew: מדהוה ליה לישראל למשחט רובא - שהיה הקנה שלם לפניו:
Rashi on Chullin 19b:11:2.english: Since the Jew should have slaughtered the majority - For the windpipe was intact before him.

Rashi on Chullin 19b:11:3.hebrew: ולא שחט - אלא חציו, לאו מידי עבד, דחיותא בחצי קנה לא נפקא, והוה ליה כקנה שלם, וכי אתא עובד כוכבים בתריה דמי כמאן דעביד כולה, דהא חיותא בידיה נפקא:
Rashi on Chullin 19b:11:3.english: And he did not slaughter - Only half of it. He did nothing [of significance], since life does not depart through half of the windpipe, and it is as if it were a whole windpipe [still intact]. And when the idolater comes after him, it is considered as though he performed all of it [the slaughter], since the life departed through his hand.

Rashi on Chullin 19b:11:4.english: But here - Where he slaughtered and struck a hole:

Rashi on Chullin 19b:11:5.english: Since he has slaughtered - Everything found in it, and a treifa [from a puncture] in half of the windpipe does not count, and initially it is like a whole windpipe, and behold it has been cut before us. What difference does it make to me whether it is in the place of the perforation, etc.:

Rashi on Chullin 19b:12:1.english: One who slaughters from the sides - On the side of the neck.

Rashi on Chullin 19b:12:2.hebrew: שחיטתו כשרה - ואפי' לכתחלה נמי. ואיידי דבעי למתני המולק מן הצדדין, תנא נמי השוחט בדיעבד:
Rashi on Chullin 19b:12:2.english: His slaughter is valid - Even ab initio as well. And since [the Tanna] wanted to teach [the case of] one who performs melikah from the sides, he also taught [the case of] one who slaughters after the fact.

Rashi on Chullin 19b:12:3.hebrew: המולק מן הצדדין מליקתו פסולה - דבמליקה כתיב "ממול ערפו", דהיינו מאחוריו:
Rashi on Chullin 19b:12:3.english: One who performs melika from the sides, his melika is invalid - For with regard to melika it is written "from opposite its nape" (Leviticus 5:8), which means from behind it.

Rashi on Chullin 19b:12:4.hebrew: השוחט מן העורף - ממול העורף מוקי לה בגמרא, כלומר מאחורי הצואר:
Rashi on Chullin 19b:12:4.english: One who slaughters from the nape - The Gemara explains it as [meaning] opposite the nape, that is, from behind the neck.

Rashi on Chullin 19b:12:5.hebrew: שחיטתו פסולה - ובגמרא מוקמינן לה בשלא החזיר הסימנין אחורי העורף, אלא חתך המפרקת עד שהגיע לסימנין, וקודם שהגיע לסימנין נטרפה בשבירת המפרקת. ואע"ג דבמליקה כשרה, התם הוא דכולה מתחילה ועד סוף הוי מן המליקה, והוי כשאר שוחט שנוקב את הוושט מעט מעט עד שגומרת שחיטתה. אבל שוחט מן העורף, כיון דשחיטה לאו הכי גמירי, לא הוי שבירת המפרקת מן השחיטה, ואיטרפא לה. והשוחט מן הצדדין דקתני רישא, אפי' בדלא אהדר, דהא מישחטי סימנין שפיר קודם חתיכת מפרקת:
Rashi on Chullin 19b:12:5.english: Its slaughter is invalid - And in the Gemara we establish it as a case where he did not turn the windpipe and gullet around to the back of the neck, but rather cut through the spinal column until he reached the windpipe and gullet, and before he reached the windpipe and gullet, it became a *tereifa* through the breaking of the spinal column. And although in *melika* [the bird] is valid, there the entire process, from beginning to end, is part of the *melika*, and it is like any other slaughterer who pierces the gullet little by little until he completes its slaughter. But one who slaughters from the nape, since we have learned that slaughter is not done this way, the breaking of the spinal column is not part of the slaughter, and [the animal] became a *tereifa*. And the one who slaughters from the sides, which the first clause of the mishna teaches, [is valid] even if he did not turn them around, since the windpipe and gullet are properly slaughtered before the spinal column is cut.

Rashi on Chullin 19b:12:6.hebrew: המולק מן העורף - וחתך בשר ומפרקת עד שהגיע לסימנין:
Rashi on Chullin 19b:12:6.english: One who nips from the nape - And he cut through flesh and the neck vertebra until he reached the windpipe and gullet.

Rashi on Chullin 19b:12:7.hebrew: מליקתו כשרה - דזו היא מצות מליקתו לכתחלה, וכדתניא לקמן (חולין דף כא.) בברייתא: חותך שדרה ומפרקת בלא רוב בשר עד שמגיע לוושט או לקנה כו'. ואיידי דתנא "השוחט מן העורף פסולה" דאפי' בדיעבד, תנא נמי "המולק" בדיעבד:
Rashi on Chullin 19b:12:7.english: Its pinching is valid - For this is the mitzvah of its pinching ab initio, and as it was taught later (Chullin 21a) in a baraita: One cuts the spine and the neck bone without [cutting] most of the flesh, until he reaches the esophagus or the windpipe, etc. And since [the mishna] taught "One who slaughters from the nape, it is invalid," [which is so] even after the fact, it also taught "One who pinches" [as valid] after the fact.

Rashi on Chullin 19b:12:8.hebrew: השוחט מן הצואר - תחת הגרון קרי צואר, והיא דרך רוב השחיטות:
Rashi on Chullin 19b:12:8.english: One who slaughters from the neck - The area beneath the throat is called the "neck," and this is the way most slaughters are performed.

Rashi on Chullin 19b:12:9.english: And the entire nape - The entire area opposite the nape:

Rashi on Chullin 19b:13:1.hebrew: אי נימא עורף ממש - מה שיש מן העורף אחורי הפרצוף קרי עורף, כדיליף לקמן בסמוך "להדי פנים", כנגד פנים:
Rashi on Chullin 19b:13:1.english: If we say ["oref" means] the actual nape - That which is part of the neck behind the face is called "oref," as [the Gemara] derives shortly below, [from the words] "directly facing the face" — opposite the face.

Rashi on Chullin 19b:13:2.hebrew: כדקתני סיפא וכל העורף כשר למליקה - ואי בעורף ממש, מאי "כל העורף"? והרי דבר מועט הוא! אלא שמע מינה, מול עורף קאמר, שהוא ארוך:
Rashi on Chullin 19b:13:2.english: As the latter clause teaches: "And the entire nape is valid for melika" - But if [it means] the actual nape, what is [the meaning of] "the entire nape"? It is a small thing! Rather, learn from this that it means the area facing the nape, which is long.

Rashi on Chullin 19b:14:1.hebrew: והוא יושב ממולי - אלמא, כל היכא דכתיב "מול", לאו עליו ממש הוא, אלא בראייתו. דהא לאו עליו ממש היו יושבים, אלא בראייתו, שהיה בלק רואה אותם:
Rashi on Chullin 19b:14:1.english: "And he is sitting opposite me" - Evidently, wherever "opposite" (*mul*) is written, it does not mean directly upon it, but rather within sight of it. For they were not sitting directly upon him, but rather within his sight, as Balak could see them:

Rashi on Chullin 19b:14:2.hebrew: עורף ולא פנים - מדכתיב "עורף" ולא פנים, ולא כתיב "כי פנו אלי עורף", ולא צואר, דהיינו גרון, ש"מ עורף דקרא לאו כנגד הגרון הוא, אלא כנגד הפנים; ומול הרואה את העורף הוי כנגד הגרון:
Rashi on Chullin 19b:14:2.english: The nape and not the face - Since it is written "nape" and not "face," and it is not written "for they turned to Me the nape," and not the neck, which is the throat, [we learn] from this that the "nape" of the verse is not opposite the throat, but opposite the face; and the place facing one who sees the nape is opposite the throat.

Rashi on Chullin 19b:14:3.hebrew: מאי ואומר - הא נפקא ליה שפיר מ"והוא יושב ממולי", ומהאי קרא בתרא לא משתמע דמול עורף דקרא לאו עורף ממש הוא, דהאי קרא לא משמע לן אלא מקום עורף היכא:
Rashi on Chullin 19b:14:3.english: What is [the point of] "and it says"? - [The meaning of "mul"] is derived well enough from "and he sits opposite me" (mimmuli); and from this latter verse it cannot be understood that "mul oref" in the verse ["mul arafo"] does not mean the actual back of the neck, for this verse teaches us only where the place of the neck is.

Rashi on Chullin 19b:14:4.hebrew: ומשני הכי קאמר וכי תימא - כלומר, אם תאמר השתא דאמרת דקרא היינו רואה את העורף, אכתי לא ידעינן עורף מאי ניהו, דנדע מול דידיה היכא:
Rashi on Chullin 19b:14:4.english: And [the Gemara] answers: This is what it is saying: And if you say - That is, if you say: Now that you have said that the verse means "facing the nape," we still do not know what the nape is, such that we would know where the area "opposite" it is.

Rashi on Chullin 19b:15:1.hebrew: מחזיר סימנין כו' - וחותך הסימנין לבדן. ולקמיה מותיב לה ממתניתין:
Rashi on Chullin 19b:15:1.english: He turns the simanim around, etc. - And he cuts the simanim [the windpipe and gullet] by themselves. And later [the Gemara] raises an objection to it from our mishna.

Rashi on Chullin 19b:15:2.hebrew: אף מחזיר - מצותו למלוק שדרה ומפרקת כולה תחלה, עד שמגיע לסימנין; ואם החזיר הסימנין ומלקן לבדן, אף זו היא מצותה:
Rashi on Chullin 19b:15:2.english: Even one who turns back - His commandment is to pinch [the neck through] the entire spine and neck-vertebra first, until he reaches the windpipe and gullet. And if he turned the windpipe and gullet around and pinched them alone, this too is his [proper fulfillment of the] commandment.

Rashi on Chullin 19b:15:3.hebrew: ואיכא דאמרי דוקא מחזיר - ואם לא החזיר אלא חתך השדרה, פסולה:
Rashi on Chullin 19b:15:3.english: And there are those who say: specifically if he turns [the signs around] - But if he did not turn them around, and merely cut the spine, [the melika] is invalid.

Rashi on Chullin 19b:16:1.hebrew: ומסתברא כמ"ד - דבני ר' חייא אף מחזיר אמרו, דאי דוקא מחזיר אמרו, הויא מתני' תיובתייהו, דקתני השוחט מן העורף כו':
Rashi on Chullin 19b:16:1.english: And it is reasonable like the one who says - That the sons of R. Chiyya said [their ruling] even of one who turns [the signs around]. For if they said it specifically of one who turns [the signs around], the mishna would be a refutation of them, as it teaches: "One who slaughters from the nape..."

Rashi on Chullin 19b:1:1.hebrew: דא"כ מפסדת לקמייתא - דאמרת משמיה דרב, הגרים שליש ושחט שליש והגרים שליש כשרה. אלמא לאו ברובא דשחיטה תליא, אלא דניפוק חיותא בשחיטה, דהיינו שליש האמצע:
Rashi on Chullin 19b:1:1.english: For if so, you invalidate the first [statement] - For you said in the name of Rav: If he cut through a third, then slaughtered a third, and then cut through a third, it is valid. Evidently, it does not depend on the majority of the slaughter, but rather on the life being expelled through the slaughter, which is the middle third.

Rashi on Chullin 19b:1:2.hebrew: הכא נמי - במיפק חיותא בעי למיתלי, ובהגרמה נפקא. וכל הנך הגרים דקאמרי רב הונא ורב יהודה הכא, לאו בהגרמה דרבנן ור' יוסי קאמרי, ולא אפלוגתייהו קיימי. דא"כ, קשיא דרב הונא אדרב הונא, דאפי' בהגרים שליש ושחט שני שלישי טריף רב הונא לעיל לדברי הכל, וכ"ש בהגרים שליש ושחט שליש והגרים שליש. אלא ההיא אפלוגתא דרבנן ורבי יוסי קיימא, ורב הונא משמיה דרב אסי קאמר לה. והא אמוגרמת דשיפוי כובע קיימי כרבי חנינא, ורב הונא משמיה דרב קאמר לה:
Rashi on Chullin 19b:1:2.english: Here too - He wants to attribute [the death] to the animal's [life-force] leaving, and it left through [an act of] hagrama (causing something indirectly). And all these instances of hagrama that Rav Huna and Rav Yehuda are speaking of here are not speaking of the hagrama of the Rabbis and Rabbi Yosei, and they do not rest on their dispute. For if so, there would be a contradiction of Rav Huna against Rav Huna: for above, even in the case where one [first] did hagrama on a third and then slaughtered two thirds, Rav Huna declares [the animal] forbidden according to everyone, and all the more so where one did hagrama on a third, slaughtered a third, and did hagrama on a third. Rather, that [ruling of Rav Huna above] rests on the dispute of the Rabbis and Rabbi Yosei, and Rav Huna says it in the name of Rav Asi. But this [ruling about the] hagrama of the raised edge of a hat rests on [the view of] Rabbi Chanina, and Rav Huna says it in the name of Rav.

Rashi on Chullin 19b:2:1.hebrew: לאו היינו דרבי אלעזר כו' - דשחיטה זו יש לה שינים כמסרק:
Rashi on Chullin 19b:2:1.english: Is this not the same as [the case of] Rabbi Elazar, etc. - For this slaughter has teeth like a comb.

Rashi on Chullin 19b:3:1.english: And perhaps [he slaughtered] in the place of slaughter - That is what he [Rabbi Elazar] is validating. But with *hagrama* outside the place of slaughter, Rabbi Elazar bar Menyumi does not validate it:

Rashi on Chullin 19b:3:2.hebrew: מפורעת - מגולה ונכרת, כמו (במדבר ה) "ופרע את ראש האשה":
Rashi on Chullin 19b:3:2.english: Unkempt - Uncovered and cut off (i.e., separated), as in (Numbers 5) "and he shall uncover the head of the woman."

Rashi on Chullin 19b:5:1.hebrew: ויתיב וקאמר כו' - רב כהנא קא בעי לה מרב יהודה:
Rashi on Chullin 19b:5:1.english: And he was sitting and saying, etc. - Rav Kahana was asking it of Rav Yehuda:

Rashi on Chullin 19b:5:2.hebrew: שחיטתו כשרה - משום דרובא בשחיטה, ורב יהודה לאו במיפק חיותא תלי טעמא, כדאמר לעיל:
Rashi on Chullin 19b:5:2.english: His slaughter is valid - Because the majority [of the cut] is in the slaughtering, and Rav Yehuda does not base his reasoning on the departure of life, as [the Gemara] said above.

Rashi on Chullin 19b:7:1.hebrew: שחט במקום נקב - שהיה חצי קנה פגום בצדו החיצון:
Rashi on Chullin 19b:7:1.english: He slaughtered in the place of a perforation - Where half of the windpipe was damaged on its outer side.

Rashi on Chullin 19b:8:1.hebrew: שחט ופגע בו נקב - שהיה חצי קנה פגום בצדו הפנימי לצד המפרקת:
Rashi on Chullin 19b:8:1.english: He slaughtered and a perforation struck it - That half of the windpipe was damaged on its inner side, on the side facing the neck vertebrae.

Tosafot on Chullin 19b:12:1.hebrew: השוחט מן הצדדין - מצינן למימר דוקא דיעבד, ואפי' החזיר סירוגין, גזירה אטו לא החזיר; ובקונטרס לא פירש כן:
Tosafot on Chullin 19b:12:1.english: One who slaughters from the sides - We can say that [the Mishnah means] specifically after the fact (di'avad), and even if he returned [the knife] intermittently (sirugin), [it is disqualified] as a decree lest one come to [treat it like a case where] he did not return [the knife at all]. And Rashi (in the Kuntres) did not explain it this way:

Tosafot on Chullin 19b:16:1.hebrew: מסתברא כמאן דאמר אף מחזיר - תימה, דלא הוה ליה למימר "מסתברא", דהא תיובתא גמורה היא ממתני' למ"ד מחזיר דוקא! ויש לומר, דלכתחלה פליגי, אבל לכולי עלמא בדיעבד כשרה בכל ענין; ולהכי קאמר "מסתברא", דהמולק מן העורף משמע כדין מליקה לכתחלה, שהיא מן העורף:
Tosafot on Chullin 19b:16:1.english: It is reasonable [to follow] the one who says that even turning [the simanim around] [is valid] - It is puzzling: [the Gemara] should not have said "it is reasonable," for this is a decisive refutation from the Mishnah of the one who says that [the mitzvah of melikah is] specifically by turning [the simanim around]! And one can say that they dispute only [the case of] *lekhatchilah* (ab initio), but according to all, *bediavad* (after the fact) it is valid in every case; and therefore [the Gemara] says "it is reasonable," because [the Mishnah's phrase] "one who performs melikah from the nape" implies the proper manner of melikah *lekhatchilah*, which is from the nape:

Tosafot on Chullin 19b:7:1.hebrew: שחט במקום נקב מהו - תימה, פשיטא דכשרה, מידי דהוה אחצי קנה פגום וגמרו! וי"ל דלא נקטיה אלא משום דבעי למיבעי אחריתי:
Tosafot on Chullin 19b:7:1.english: If he slaughtered at the place of a perforation, what is the law? - It is astonishing: it is obvious that it is valid, just like [the case of] half of the windpipe that was damaged and he finished [the slaughter]! And one can answer that [the Gemara] mentions it only because it wants to ask another [question]:

Tosafot on Chullin 19b:8:1.hebrew: שחט ופגע בו נקב מהו אמר ליה טרפה - ולא דמי לשחט שליש והגרים שליש ושחט שליש, דכשרה לרב יהודה גופיה, דהתם שלא במקום שחיטה. אבל שחט במקום נקב עדיף טפי, לפי שהוא במקום שחיטה, מהגרים שליש ושחט שליש. הריב"א:
Tosafot on Chullin 19b:8:1.english: [If] he slaughtered and encountered a perforation in it, what is the ruling? He said to him: It is a treifa - And this is not comparable to [a case where] he slaughtered a third, [then] pressed [the knife] a third, and slaughtered [another] third, which is valid even according to Rav Yehuda himself, for there [the pressing was] not in the place of slaughter. But [where] he slaughtered in the place of a perforation, it is more [problematic] than [a case of] pressing a third and slaughtering a third, because it is in the place of slaughter. [This is the view of] the Ri"v (Rabbi Isaac ben Asher, the Riva).
